title: Dea title in poems and prose—Lipsius, Mendoza, Catharinus, Bembo; Bustis prefer ‘Queen of mercy’
source_text: LXVII. Neque solum omnium Domina & Regina in Ecclesia Romana Sancta Virgo dicitur, sed ipsum Deae nomen a multis illi tribuitur. Frequens id est in sacris eorum Poematis, ut in illo Lipsii, Hae tibi laudes Dea dicet omnis, Sexus & aetas. Item, An sudat Dea sanguinem hoc in aevo. Et in illo Caesaris, Nec terra ad superos trade Dea calle secundo, & pluribus aliis. Sed & illi qui scribunt oratione soluta non raro Deae nomen Beatae Virgini tribuunt. Sic Mendoza Jesuita dicit, per Orationem Virginem fieri universae tanquam Deam creaturae. Sic Philippus Beroaldus, Quid majus, inquit, in laudem Deae nostrae dicitur, quam quod materno affectu & indulgentia nos foveat? Sic Ambrosius Catharinus unus ex Patribus Synodi Tridentinae, aliquid ex Augustino citans, Verbum protulit, inquit, Augustinus pro Domina Dea nostra, quod non pigebit referre. Verum, Non hominem dici eam sit fas quae mater est Dei, quae amicta sole & coronata duodecim stellis lunam habet sub pedibus. O Dea certe quae adeo particeps fuisti divinitatis, ut sola servata sis tanquam paradisus Dei, Dei manibus excolendus. Quin ipse Cardinalis Bembus nomine Leonis X. ad quandam Italiae civitatem scribens, monet ut meliora ligna in usum aedis Lauretanae donent, Ne tum nos, inquit, tum etiam Deam ipsam, indigna inutilium lignorum donatione lusisse videamini. Antoninus vero & Bernardinus de Bustis, saepe Beatam Virginem Deam Dearum recte dici posse, sed in solatium peccatorum, eam tamen dici malunt Reginam misericordiae.
pass_a_gloss: Nor is the Holy Virgin said in the Roman Church only Lady and Queen of all, but the very name Goddess is attributed to her by many. That is frequent in their sacred Poems, as in that of Lipsius: Every sex and age will speak these praises to thee, Goddess. Likewise, Or does the Goddess sweat blood in this age. And in that of Caesar: Nor on earth hand over, Goddess, by a second path to the gods above, and in many others. But also those who write in unbound speech not rarely attribute the name Goddess to the Blessed Virgin. Thus Mendoza the Jesuit says that through Prayer the Virgin becomes as it were Goddess of every creature. Thus Philip Beroaldus: What greater thing, he says, is said in praise of our Goddess than that she fosters us with maternal affection and indulgence? Thus Ambrosius Catharinus, one of the Fathers of the Tridentine Synod, citing something from Augustine, says Augustine uttered a word for our Lady Goddess which it will not irk to report. Truly, Let it not be lawful that she be called a human who is mother of God, who clothed with the sun and crowned with twelve stars has the moon under her feet. O Goddess certainly who wast so far partaker of divinity that thou alone wast kept as paradise of God, to be cultivated by the hands of God. Nay Cardinal Bembo himself, writing in the name of Leo X to a certain city of Italy, warns that they give better wood for the use of the Loreto shrine, Lest then, he says, both we and even the Goddess herself seem to have been mocked by an unworthy donation of useless woods. But Antoninus and Bernardinus de Bustis often say that the Blessed Virgin can rightly be called Goddess of Goddesses, yet for the consolation of sinners they prefer that she be called Queen of mercy.
pass_b_english: Many even give Mary the name Goddess—in verse (Lipsius) and prose (Mendoza, Beroaldus, Catharinus).
Bembo for Leo X speaks of ‘the Goddess’ at Loreto; Bustis allow ‘Goddess of Goddesses’ but prefer Queen of mercy.
